reason: The complete definition is available and supports multiple meaning and application diagnostics. However, Section 14.5 redacts the duration that triggers the Parties' mandatory good-faith discussion of modifications for persistent Force Majeure. This is an essential operative rule for applying the term over time, so a complete closed set of six meaning/use diagnostics and concrete application questions is not eligible under the stated completeness requirement. The missing duration cannot be inferred from the source.

The complete definition includes a mixed-request allocation rule omitted from the supplied extraction. However, a source-closed set of six meaning/use diagnostics and concrete application questions is not eligible: essential scope and exclusion definitions—Deployed Products, Structured Negotiations Product, and Vert-General Release Enhancement—are incorporated from the Subscription License Agreement, which is not supplied. Exhibits A, B, and C are present, but they do not cure those missing definitions. Limited questions about mixed requests and response standards are possible, but the full product boundary and Enhancement exclusion cannot be resolved from this source alone.

The complete definition supplies a worldwide baseline and express geographic and cruise-ship exclusions without depending on a missing exhibit or redacted rule. A useful closed set of six diagnostics can address ordinary included locations, the United States exclusion, the Caribbean exclusion, ships based at United States ports, ships based at Caribbean ports, and the distinction between territorial distribution rights and the express Las Vegas exhibition obligation. The separate distribution agreement preserved by Section 19 is not supplied, so questions about its rights or interaction with exclusivity should be excluded; it is not needed to apply the express Territory definition.

The complete definition and the identities of both excluded entities are available without redaction. A useful closed set of six diagnostics can address the two named-party exclusions, separate affiliated entities, unrelated entities, lawful third-party information disclosures under Section 9.3(b), and transaction-related disclosures under Section 12. These classification and application questions do not require the redacted Project Plans, Appendix B sequences, or the unavailable Quality Agreement. Questions about the specific products covered by Sections 5.13 and 5.15 or preauthorized subcontractors would require unavailable material and should not be included.

A useful closed set of six diagnostics is possible on authorization types, necessity for the listed activities, jurisdictional relevance, qualifying governmental authorities, the express NHI Price Listing exclusion, and the distinction between an application and an obtained approval in the pre-sale restriction. The definition and these dependencies are unredacted. The absent substantive Regulatory Plan and redacted milestone, diligence, and timing provisions are not essential to this bounded set; questions requiring those materials should not be included.

The complete definition and its pricing and reimbursement exclusions are available. However, essential application rules are not fully disclosed: Section 4.4(b), which supplies the Special Access Approval definition and qualifies the allocation of regulatory responsibilities, is entirely redacted. Section 7.3 expressly connects Special Access Approval with other Regulatory Approval. The Field definition governing Product scope is also redacted, and Section 4.2 redacts material conditions for removing countries from the Territory. The Product definition additionally uses 'Drug Approval' without a disclosed definition. Narrow classification questions are possible, but a sufficiently source-resolved closed set of six meaning/use diagnostics and concrete applications is not supported without assuming missing rules.

The complete definition and the operative ownership, use, copying, and return rules are present in Section 2.17. Section 2.12 supplies the contrasting treatment of other documentation and concrete examples of reports. A useful closed set of six diagnostics can address classification of maintenance instructions, corrections and enhancements, exclusion of delivered data and reports, retained ownership versus limited use, copying with prior written consent, and return of originals and copies on termination. No missing exhibit or redacted rule is essential to these diagnostics; the redacted financial provisions and omitted Appendix A are not needed.

The complete definition is supplied in Exhibit A, which Article I expressly incorporates for this term. A useful closed set of six diagnostics is possible: ordinary weekday inclusion, weekend exclusion, banking-holiday exclusion, facsimile receipt timing, invoice payment rollover, and the financial-assurance response period. Concrete applications can stipulate weekday and banking-holiday status. No essential exhibit or rule for those applications is missing or redacted.

The complete definition is available and includes a second sentence extending the term to qualifying post-Effective-Date agreements. However, that extension expressly depends on Section 14.5, whose acquisition conditions, response deadline, and material payment rules are redacted. The Imigen license requirements incorporated by Sections 14.5.3–14.5.4 are also not supplied. Basic classification questions are possible, but the source does not support the requested closed set of six meaning/use diagnostics and concrete applications without relying on missing essential rules.

A useful closed set of six diagnostics is possible: registered copyrights, unregistered copyrights, copyright applications, the scope of the Trademark exclusion, exclusive-use versus historical-use classification under the Arizona copyright definitions, and Company-owned copyrights used in the Arizona Field. Concrete applications can stipulate ownership, use, and timing without requiring an asset inventory. The complete definition and the definition governing its exclusion are present. Exhibit A's trademark license text and the incorporated Stock Purchase Agreement are not supplied, but neither is essential to this bounded set; questions requiring their additional rules should be excluded.

The complete definition and relevant application clauses are present. A useful closed set of six diagnostics can cover ordinary weekdays, nonholiday Saturdays, ordinary Sundays, recognized holidays outside the four exceptions, the four expressly included holidays, and application of Processing Day versus following Business Day to the BIC update deadline. Concrete scenarios can stipulate weekday and Federal Reserve holiday status without requiring an external holiday calendar. The redacted schedules and provisions are not essential to these diagnostics.

The complete definition and the relevant service and theatre provisions are supplied, including Exhibits A, B and D. A useful closed set of six diagnostics can address: (1) collected versus merely billed advertising revenue; (2) refunds and similar disbursements; (3) applicable taxes and governmental charges versus ordinary income tax; (4) exhibition in covered Theatres and the treatment of Excluded Theatres; (5) direct and indirect Network Affiliate receipts connected with the Service and alternative or independent digital film distribution; and (6) application of the stated 50% advertising revenue share to a concrete qualifying-revenue calculation. No missing exhibit or redacted rule is essential to that set. The accounting sentence refers to Section 8.3, which actually concerns termination by NCM; that cross-reference should not be treated as supplying additional accounting rules.

A useful closed set of six diagnostics is possible: coverage of direct employees; coverage of entity contractors and agents; coverage of the specified persons' individual employees, contractors and other agents; Affiliate status through direct, indirect or common control; the express cross-group Affiliate exclusion; and application of the Personnel assignment obligation in Section 8.2(b) to a qualifying development. The definition is complete and unredacted. The omitted attachments are not essential to these diagnostics. The Separation Agreement is not supplied, so questions should stipulate Spinco/Pluto Group membership rather than require identification of actual group members; likewise, no question should depend on an unseen Facility Addendum or policy.

The complete definition and relevant product-category provisions are present. A useful closed set of six diagnostics can address the ICS alias, the corticosteroid requirement, the inclusive 24-hour threshold, the clinical-testing requirement, classification of a qualifying ICS combined with an expressly accepted Pooled Compound for respiratory treatment or prophylaxis, and the exclusion of ICS as the other active agent specified in the Other Combination Product definition. These questions require no missing exhibit or redacted rule.

Section 15 supplies the complete definition, confidentiality and use restrictions, and all stated exceptions without relying on missing exhibits or redacted rules. Section 13.2 supplies survival. A closed set of six useful diagnostics and concrete applications can cover: (1) covered information and permitted use/disclosure, (2) public-domain exceptions, (3) prior possession and rightful third-party receipt, (4) independent development, (5) tangible marking and timely written confirmation of oral disclosure, and (6) compelled disclosure and notice. The redacted pricing, quantities, and commission rate are not essential to these diagnostics.

Section 23.3 supplies the complete definition, an express financing/payment exclusion, and self-contained conditions for relief. A useful closed set of six diagnostics and concrete applications can address covered events, the financing/payment exclusion, causal prevention or hindrance or delay, reasonable commercial measures and best efforts, the extent and duration of relief, and notice requirements. No missing exhibit or redacted rule is essential to these questions.
